findings.text: Fix 2 breaks the "fallback wrote first" guarantee for a real tab. `RecordWriter.post` now sends `client` on every verb (`core/Item/RecordWriter.js:56`), but the stamped lines it hands back as `rest` for the fallback carry no `client` (line 51). So the line the tab appends through `Append.js` is keyed `owner|ts`, while the late post is checked with `c:<client>|ts` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:149`). They never match, the late post writes a second line, and `doc/one-writer.md:231` ("the late post is answered `{already: true}`") is no longer true. `one-writer.test.mjs:103` still passes only because its late verb is posted without a `client`, which no real tab does any more. The fix: put `client` on the verb lines in `list` too, so the fallback line carries it, and add a case 3 variant that uses the real tab shape.

Fix 1 says "newline guard before **every** append" (fixes.md 1), and `core/doc/status.md`'s Phase 0 row now says "Done". But only `RecordWriter.append_once` has the guard. The two main append paths still append blind: the entry point's `write_line` (`Servex/agents/page_tools.js:183`, used by every `record_lines` and item-tool write) and the dev server's fallback (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Append.js:131`). Either add the guard there with a test, or change the status row to say what is really covered.

Fix 5 changes the on-disk shape of every browser `List.add`: fields now sit under `data` instead of flat (`core/List/List.js:254-263`). Nobody checked the readers that read an `add` payload flat instead of through `hydrate()`. Examples: `ai/rail/rail.js:484` (`fold.content?.add?.text ?? …title`), `ai/cards/Activity.js:143` and `ai/AISession/SessionTimelineRows.js:97`. A card added to a page's content list from the browser would now show blank in those summaries. Do the census, then fix each reader or say why it can't receive these lines.

The F4 helper is a static on `Runtime` (`Server/plugins/SocketServer/Runtime.js:50`), and `rpc:write` is its only caller. fixes.md asks for "one crash-safe rewrite helper". Other rewriters still truncate in place: `Server/SessionConsolidate.mjs:110,132` uses plain `writeFileSync`. Consider moving the helper somewhere shared and listing its callers in status.md.

`safe_write` creates a `<file>.tmp-<pid>-<ms>` sibling inside the watched `public/` tree. LiveReload mutes only the real path (`Runtime.js:36`), so every save also queues a change for the tmp path, which is sent to every tab (`LiveReload.js:143-185`). That is probably harmless, because tabs ignore paths they didn't load, but it hasn't been checked.

Fix 2's second clause in fixes.md ("the item tool's own stamps repeat too (the flaky one-writer test)") is not addressed or mentioned. Fix 3 is marked "already built" with no test. The brief allows the skip, but status.md should link to the code that proves it (`ext/JSONL/live.js`, the `Socket.prototype.open` override).

findings.text: `PromptItem` is never registered, so a Prompt card's items do not survive a snapshot (step 6). `core/Session/Chat/PromptItem.js` has no `Item.register(PromptItem, "PromptItem")`, yet `toJSON()` writes `"type":"PromptItem"`. I checked in the worktree: replay a Prompt with one item, then `Session.hydrate(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(s.toJSON())))`. It warns `unknown type "PromptItem" — preserved as Item`, and the item comes back as a plain `Item`, which has no `push_sentences`, so a later `{sentences:{push}}` replaces the array instead of growing it. Add the register line, and add a snapshot round trip of `items` to `Chat.test.mjs`. The existing round trip in `chat-messages.test.mjs:96` runs before any item exists.

`Prompt.raw.test.mjs:336` cannot fail on the thing it claims to check (step 5, "every Sentence carries `at`"). `expected` falls back to `?? s.text`, so a sentence with no `at`, or an `at` that matches no V1 line, compares its own text with itself and passes. Nothing asserts that `at` is present. The data is fine today (I counted 33 sentences, 33 with `at`, 33 matched to an owner `{chat}` line), but the test would not catch a regression. Assert `s.at` and `owner_chat_by_at.has(s.at)` for every sentence, and drop the fallback.

A fresh agent could not tell from `session.jsonl` which steps landed. Child task `s3` is still only `start`ed, and `s4`, `s5` and `s6` have no start or complete line. The `sent` mark on the message relies on `ChatWriter.message_for`, which is memory only (`msg_at`). Also, only the `smart` seat is tested (`chat-messages.test.mjs`, step 5/6 block); `fast` goes through the same code at `Sessions.js:1089` and `:1248`.

`fixture/v-u48msei-session.jsonl` is an 805 KB, 1,737-line copy of a real session. Only the last 33 mirrored sentences are tested. A trimmed tail (the mirrored part plus its `{chat}` lines) would test the same thing, keep the repo small, and carry less of the owner's dictation into `public/`.

findings.text: The "V1 way" in `V1Bubbles.js:152` (`bubbles()`) does not match what V1 actually draws. `ext/Chat/Chat.js:58-70` `place()` moves every new bubble before any bubble with a later `at` (`said_at`), so V1 shows bubbles in time order, while the mirror keeps file order. That makes `doc/pseudo-properties.md:248` wrong too: it says V1 draws "in file order" and blames the 1114/591 differing bubbles on the reply hold. Mirror `place()` in the reader, re-run the compare, and only then write down the cause.

`doc/pseudo-properties.md:247` contradicts `s8/compare.txt`. It says "every session but `v-timqv56` needed it", but compare.txt:2532 shows `v-timqv56` was also built by `plan()`. The one session that did not need `plan()` is `v-u48msei`. Rewrite the sentence from the real numbers: 4 of 5 were planned, and `v-u48msei` is only partly mirrored.

The step-2 gate ("0 sessions still needing `ChatToMessages.plan()`", `doc/pseudo-properties.md:247`) can't be measured by the tool. `ChatV1Compare.mjs:55` treats any file with a single `messages`/`sentences` line as fully mirrored, so `v-u48msei` (278 V1 bubbles against 63 from the adapter) would already pass the gate. The tool should count `{chat}` lines that have no mirror (as `Prompt.raw.test.mjs` already does: 33 of 152), or the gate should be reworded.

The readme's "Check it" section (`core/Session/Chat/readme.md:69-74`) doesn't list `node public/framework/core/Session/Chat/V1Bubbles.test.mjs` (4 checks, which pass) or `node Server/ChatV1Compare.mjs`. Each file there is indexed under "Check it", so the new test and tool should be too (Law 10). The only mention is the ✅ line at readme:92.

`ChatV1Compare.mjs:58-61` writes the lines to an OS temp file and then reads them straight back before calling `ChatToMessages.plan()`. `plan(lines)` gives the same result with no file, so the round trip only adds disk writes. The brief also named the session scratchpad, not `os.tmpdir()`.

The fixture check in `V1Bubbles.test.mjs:222-224` (owner pieces = sentences) is true by construction, because `events()` pushes each sentence exactly once. It can't catch a merge bug. A V1-against-adapter comparison on the mirrored tail of the fixture would test something real.

The `fix` handling in `V1Bubbles.js:142` only partly matches V1. V1 (`Chat.js:787-791`) replaces the original piece's text with the fix text, but the mirror drops the fix line and keeps the old text. Fixed lines will therefore show up as text differences that V1 never draws. The header comment (`V1Bubbles.js:109-113`) covers `fix` only for bubble counts, not text.
`Server/doc/scripts.md` (the census of `Server/` scripts) has no row for `Server/ChatV1Compare.mjs`, although `ChatToMessages.mjs` has one at line 52.
